An '''alphabet''' was used on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="SWR" /> by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]],<ref name="Date">The unidentified alphabet was featured in the video game ''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]'', the events of which occurred eight years after the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] annual [[Podracing/Legends|Podrace]] shown in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. According to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', the events of ''The Phantom Menace'' happened in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> when that world was under the domination of [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] such as [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> and [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla Besadii the Elder]].<ref name="FF127">{{FactFile|127|HUT 5-8|Gardulla the Hutt}}</ref> It comprised twenty-six letters, each of which had its exact equivalent in the [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]].<ref name="SWI35">{{InsiderCite|35|Making Special Edition Collectibles}}</ref> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it also saw use on [[Talus/Legends|Talus]], a planet of the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]].<ref name="SWG">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66909&resource=features|text=''A Galaxy At War''}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The alphabet was designed by [[Eric Larson]] when the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]] came out in [[1997]]. At the time, the [[Wikipedia:PepsiCo|PepsiCo]] food corporation and its subsidiaries created several collectible promotions to coincide with the release. Among those were the pizza boxes for [[Wikipedia:Pizza Hut|Pizza Hut]], which featured secret messages written in a cipher called "Jabba's alphabet." The code key was provided in the box. Larson stated that he based his alphabet on a modern [[Wikipedia:Hebrew alphabet|Hebrew]] font after noticing similar markings on the original prop of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]],<ref name="SWI35" /> as seen in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']].<ref name="EPV">{{Film|V}}</ref>

In [[July]], [[1999]], two fans known as "Mike Dolan" and "Tommy of Escondido" crafted a typeface reproducing Eric Larson's Huttese alphabet. That font was originally available at [http://www.geocities.com Geocities.com] under the name "Trade Huttese."<ref name="Geo">{{WebCite|url=http://www.geocities.com/timessquare/4965/sffont.html#huttese|text=''Star Wars'' Nal-Huttese font|date=2009-10-04|format=HTML|archivedate=20091004032949}}</ref>

In the [[2002]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]'', that alphabet was used in the [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] selection menu. With the diversity of the playable characters' names, the entire alphabet was featured in the game, and the mapping corresponds<ref name="SWR">''[[Star Wars: Racer Revenge]]''</ref> both with Larson's<ref name="SWI35" /> and that of the "Trade Huttese" typeface.<ref name="Geo" />
